initial_observation.demographics: A Japanese infant boy weighing 1860 g was delivered by cesarean section at 36 weeks and three days
initial_observation.encounter_context: he was referred to our department on his first day of life
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The presentation of the symptoms at birth was consistent with congenital CMV infection, which was confirmed by positive CMV-DNA in urine and whole blood
presenting_symptoms: demarcation line at the temporal peripheral zone in both eyes
arteriovenous anastomosis in the right eye
known_prior_history: mother HIV-negative but had fever at four weeks of gestation
mother had positive CMV-IgG and CMV-IgM titers
diagnosed with severe symptomatic congenital CMV infection during pregnancy

evidence_items.source_text: Ophthalmoscopic examinations revealed posterior vessel dilation and a demarcation line at the temporal peripheral zone in both eyes, and an arteriovenous anastomosis in the right eye. There were no signs of chorioretinitis (Fig. 1a).

On the fourth day of life, we performed fluorescein angiography (FA) for a closer examination. The results of the FA revealed a filling delay and an arterio-venous anastomosis, but no leakage from the retinal vessels was detected. On the other hand, a small avascular zone was found at the most peripheral retina (Fig. 1b).

a sample of the aqueous humor was obtained with written informed consent, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed by SRL Inc. (Tokyo, Japan) to detect CMV-DNA in the eye. The sense and anti-sense primer sequences were TTAGTGAACCGTCAGATCGC and GCATGCATAAGAAGCCAAGG, respectively. CMV-DNA was positive in the aqueous humor (Fig. 2c).
Six days after the initiation of antiviral therapy with oral valgancyclovir, the vessel dilation regressed completely, and the arterio-venous anastomosis improved remarkably (Fig. 1c, d).
evidence_items.temporal_cue: 11 days old (6 days of antiviral therapy)

evidence_items.source_text: At three months of age, we re-examined the patient using FA. The results showed that the arterio-venous anastomosis had almost completely regressed. However, chorioretinal atrophy was found at the macula and around the optic disc (Fig. 2a, b).

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: The results established an accurate diagnosis of ocular CMV infection
